1: John writes about what the apostles heard, saw and touched: the Word of life. God is light, and in him is no darkness. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves; if we confess our sins, he is faithful and will forgive us.
The faith rests on eyewitnesses. Honesty about sin is the way to forgiveness.
2: If anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ. Whoever says he knows God but does not keep his commandments is a liar. Do not love the world. Antichrists have gone out from among us, those who deny that Jesus is the Christ.
Knowing God is shown by obeying him. Truth about who Jesus is cannot be traded away.
3: See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God. What we shall be has not yet appeared, but we shall be like him. Whoever hates his brother is a murderer. Let us love not in word but in deed and truth.
We are God's children now, and more is coming. Love is proved by action.
4: Test the spirits: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is from God. Love is from God, because God is love. He loved us first and sent his Son. Perfect love drives out fear. Whoever does not love a brother he can see cannot love God whom he cannot see.
"God is love" is the shortest summary of the faith. Love of God and love of neighbour cannot be separated.
5: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and they are not burdensome. God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. There is sin that leads to death and sin that does not.
John's distinction is one basis for the Church's teaching on mortal and venial sin. Eternal life begins now, in Christ.
